summary: The PR workflow flow is well supported: 29 of 34 claims are stated in skills/create-pr.md or AGENTS.md and none is contradicted. The partial ones simplify conditions (quality overrides, extra body sections, the DRAFT and UNVERIFIED branches). The main gaps are source steps the flow never shows: the UNVERIFIED no-local-gate path, the 30-line auto-correct limit, the /deslop pass and the Callable-unit checklist that blocks a merge.

code.overview: Most of this flow is the agent following skills/create-pr.md with git and gh; no script opens, watches or merges the PR. Code covers the edges: a session-start hook that warns when the branch is behind main, compute-bump.ts for the version, the hosted checks in .github/workflows (ci.yml, quality.yml, security.yml), check-handoff.ts before the merge, and release.yml after it. The repo has no Makefile, so the skill's `make ci` step falls through to its 'no local gate' branch here.

refs.anchor: echo "⚠  '$BRANCH' is $BEHIND commit(s) behind origin/main — merge before new feature work: git merge origin/main"
refs.title: Session-start hook: warn when the branch is behind origin/main
refs.explain: It fetches origin/main quietly and exits if the fetch fails. It reads the current branch and counts commits that origin/main has and HEAD lacks. If the count is not zero it prints a warning: pull when on main, merge origin/main otherwise.
refs.why: This covers 'pull the latest main' as a warning only; it always exits 0 and changes nothing. Cutting the fresh branch is done by the agent.

refs.anchor: "test:checks": "node scripts/check-resolvable.ts --strict && node scripts/update-skills-doc.ts --check && node scripts/check-agents-detail.ts && node scripts/check-handoff.ts && node scripts/check-guidelines.ts && node scripts/render-explorer-pages.ts --check && node scripts/render-diagrams.ts --check",
refs.title: npm test: the local test and check commands
refs.explain: test runs four parts in order and stops at the first failure: the node tests one file at a time, the tool tests, every scripts/test-*.sh, and the repo checks (resolver, skills doc, agents detail, handoff, guidelines, explorer pages, diagrams). test:integration is separate and needs RUN_INTEGRATION=1.
refs.why: These are the commands the local gates run in this repo, and the same ones CI runs. The skill looks for `make ci` or scripts/ci-local.sh first; neither exists here, so the agent runs these directly.

refs.anchor: echo "pre-commit: tsconfig.json present but tsc not installed — skipping (install deps, e.g. npm ci)" >&2
refs.title: Pre-commit hook: lint, quality check and typecheck on each commit
refs.explain: With set -eu any failing step blocks the commit. It runs ESLint on staged JS/TS files, the mechanical quality check on staged files, the whole-project tsc --noEmit, then check-resolvable and the skills-doc freshness check. Each step is skipped when its tool or file is missing.
refs.why: It catches lint and type errors before they reach the PR. It only runs when core.hooksPath is set to .githooks, which the session-start hook does for cloud sessions; locally it is opt-in.

refs.title: computeBump: next version from commit messages
refs.explain: It scans commit subject and body lines. A BREAKING CHANGE or a feat!/fix! line means major and stops the scan; a feat: line means minor; a fix: line means patch if nothing higher was seen. With no such line it returns none; otherwise it returns the bumped version string.
refs.why: The skill pipes git log origin/main..HEAD into this to pick the version it commits on the branch before pushing. The release job later tags exactly that version.

refs.title: Test: the quality gate comes before the PR body in the skill text
refs.explain: It finds the line numbers of the 'Step 5' and 'Step 6' headings in skills/create-pr.md, matching headings only. It passes when Step 5 (the quality gate) appears before Step 6 (drafting the PR body), and fails otherwise.
refs.why: This pins the order 'score 10/10 first, then open the PR' in the skill document. It checks the text of the instructions, not what an agent did; nothing in code checks the scores or the PR body.

refs.title: CI verify job: npm test on every PR to main
refs.explain: On a pull request to main, the job checks out the code without stored credentials, installs the Node version from .node-version, runs npm ci and then npm test. npm test chains the node tests, the tool tests, the shell tests and the repo checks.
refs.why: This is one of the real checks whose conclusion the agent reads on the final head. The workflow has no roll-up job, so each job's own result must be read.

refs.title: CI lint job: lint, typecheck and import boundaries
refs.explain: After checkout and npm ci it runs npm run lint (ESLint with zero warnings allowed), npm run typecheck (tsc --noEmit), then the import-boundary check. Any failing step fails the job.
refs.why: A second hosted check on the PR head, separate from the tests. A PR that passes tests but breaks types or boundaries stops here.

refs.title: Quality Gate: mechanical checks on all source files
refs.explain: On PR open, update or reopen it lists every tracked js, mjs, ts, tsx, sh, py, rb and go file. If there are any, it runs scripts/check-quality-mechanical.sh on all of them.
refs.why: This is the machine half of the quality bar; the 10/10 score from /simplify is model judgment made before the PR opens.

refs.title: Security scan: list what the PR changes and scan it for secrets
refs.explain: The fetch helper downloads a release asset and rejects it unless its sha256 matches the pinned value. The step lists files added or changed between the base tip and the PR merge commit. If any changed, it downloads gitleaks, copies the changed files to a temp tree and scans them, adding 'gitleaks' to the failed list on a finding.
refs.why: This starts the 'Security scan' check that must pass before merge. Scanning only what the PR adds keeps it fast; osv-scanner and zizmor follow in the same step when lockfiles or workflows changed.

refs.title: Security scan: zizmor on workflow changes, then fail if any scanner failed
refs.explain: If a changed path is a workflow, an action file or dependabot.yml, it downloads the pinned zizmor and runs it, recording a failure. At the end, a non-empty failed list prints an error naming the scanners and exits 1; otherwise it prints 'security scan: clean'.
refs.why: All three scanners report through this one exit, so the check's conclusion is a real pass or fail. The job runs on every pull request, so it is not skipped by a path filter.

refs.anchor: return existsSync(path) ? [`handoffs live only on branches; clear it before merging to main: git rm ${path} && git commit -m "chore: clear handoff before merge"`] : [];
refs.title: check-handoff --pre-merge: fail while a handoff file exists
refs.explain: preMerge returns an error when .pause/handoff.md exists, with the git rm command to clear it. The CLI block picks preMerge when --pre-merge is passed, else the content check. Any error is printed and the process exits 1; otherwise it prints OK.
refs.why: A handoff must not ride a merge into main, where a later /resume would act on it. The agent runs this on the head it is about to merge; nothing in CI runs the --pre-merge form.

refs.anchor: console.error('advance: requires selected completed task, no active claims, --pr <merged-pr-url> and --branch <fresh-working-branch>');
refs.title: queue advance: record the merged PR and the fresh branch
refs.explain: It refuses unless the id is the selected delivery task, that task was accepted as done, no task is active, --pr looks like a pull request URL and --branch is not empty. On success it clears deliveryTask and deliveryAccepted, saves, and writes the PR and branch to the log.
refs.why: This closes the delivery cycle so the queue will hand out the next task. The code checks only the queue's own state and the URL's shape; it does not ask GitHub whether the PR merged, so the orchestrator vouches for that.

refs.title: Release job: tag main after the merge
refs.explain: On a push to main it checks out full history and reads the version from package.json. If the tag v<version> already exists it stops. Otherwise it creates the annotated tag and pushes only the tag.
refs.why: This is the only code that runs because of the merge. It relies on the version bump already being on the PR branch, and it pushes a tag, never a commit, so main's history stays one squash commit per PR.
